name: B-p76
text: Stretch and Release: Work out what will be supporting you, focus on the feeling of support. You can also focus on where one of your hands or feet is. Either actually, or in your imagination, stretch a little bit, either stretching that part of your body slightly or pressing gently down into the support, and then let go of the effort, just relax. See if there is any difference, even if there isn’t. Do this for no more than 3 places on your body. Think of it as releasing as you go through the sequence. Which bit of your body, or voice, needs this? What do you need to support it? Bring your body back to normal movement and return.

name: B-p77
text: Supported Floating: Work out what is supporting you and where your weight is, imagine that the support is holding a tiny bit (1%) more of your effort. It’s like floating but you don’t have to lose contact, or you can just keep it at the same level, with just enough weight/pressure. See what happens, you can fractionate this if you want, perhaps noticing your normal awareness when you breathe in and the support when you breathe out. Tell yourself you are going to do this before you do it. What can you hear more easily now? Bring yourself back to normal feeling of support and return.

name: B-p78
text: Gradual wave: start with a very small neutral area, feel into it a little and then imagine a wave spreading out to a new area that is still ok. Sense into the new area (or continue using the old). See if there is anything different at each step. Does the body want any contact, space, words, other care? Let the mental image go, sense your body, sense your contact points, come back.

name: B-p79
text: Care workshop: prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc). Invite the signal/feeling/young part to come only as close as is welcome. Try to avoid any language that makes you feel you’re not one person. Care for it as best you can, by asking what it wants and giving that if you can, or sensing into it and responding, or just being with it. Take breaks, get back in contact if that’s ok, take more breaks, etc. Keep bringing in adult functions (or borrow someone else’s function). Have the adult part of you run the show. Goal is to make it “good as you” rather than “good as new”, not to erase history. Tell your little one, “That’s enough for today. We’re going back to the life we’re building.” Close the workspace, reassure yourself that you are one whole person, that you’re an adult now, and come back.
